inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: CFTR/ENaC physiology in airway vs sweat duct
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Two-panel epithelial diagram (sweat duct, airway) each showing Normal vs CF: CFTR and ENaC on the apical membrane, Cl−/Na+/H2O arrows reversing between the tissues, normal vs dehydrated mucus layers

notes: The CFTR/ENaC figure is an original KYP redraw preserving the source's four-state layout: sweat duct (Normal: Cl− reabsorbed via CFTR + Na+ via ENaC; CF: CFTR defective, Cl− trapped in sweat) and airway (Normal: Cl−/H2O secreted → hydrated mucus; CF: no secretion + ENaC-driven Na+/H2O reabsorption → dehydrated mucus), with lumen/interstitium labels and the transepithelial potential-difference note.
